title: ODSUM: Benchmarking Open Domain Multi-Document Summarization

reviews.summary: This paper introduces two new benchmarks for open-domain MDS via utilizing existing query-focused MDS datasets. They conducted extensive experiments using various approaches and found that open-domain MDS remains challenging, with significant performance drops due to retrieval errors. Human evaluations also showed that current automated metrics do not accurately reflect model performance.
reviews.strengths:
1. Proposed some new benchmarks for the evaluation of MDS for the open-domain scenarios. 
2. Conducted extensive experiments with various methods and identified limitations of existing models. 
3. Also demonstrated the limitations of various evaluation metrics for this task.
reviews.weaknesses:
1. The proposed dataset is a bit synthetic since it was developed via utilizing existing datasets, although an important new problem is studied. 
2. Also, it would have been nice to present a real-world example in the introduction section to better explain the ODSUM task.
3. The proposed methodology also lacks novelty. While it is not mandatory to propose a novel method since a new benchmark is proposed, the authors did not cite related work that utilized some of their methodologies, e.g., truncation, map-reduce, etc. [Ref1, Ref2, Ref3, Ref4]:

Ref 1: Travis Goodwin, Max Savery, and Dina Demner-Fushman. 2020. Flight of the PEGASUS? Comparing Transformers on Few-shot and Zero-shot Multi-document Abstractive Summarization. In Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Computational Linguistics, pages 5640–5646, Barcelona, Spain (Online). International Committee on Computational Linguistics.

Ref 2: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Enamul Hoque, and Jimmy Xiangji Huang. 2022. Domain Adaptation with Pre-trained Transformers for Query-Focused Abstractive Text Summarization. Computational Linguistics, 48(2):279–320.

Ref 3: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Cheng Chen, and Shashi Bhushan TN. 2023. Building Real-World Meeting Summarization Systems using Large Language Models: A Practical Perspective. In Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track, pages 343–352, Singapore. Association for Computational Linguistics.

Ref 4: Baumel, Tal, Matan Eyal, and Michael Elhadad. "Query focused abstractive summarization: Incorporating query relevance, multi-document coverage, and summary length constraints into seq2seq models." arXiv preprint arXiv:1801.07704 (2018).
reviews.questions:
Would have been nice to see how long context LLMs, e.g., LLM with 128K or longer context perform in this dataset.
